image_description: A close-up view of a grey whale's head and rostrum emerging vertically from blue ocean water. The skin is dark grey/black with distinctive white mottling and barnacle patches. The rest of the body, flippers, and tail are submerged or out of frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image shows the underside/rostrum of the whale vertically. The top of the head where blowholes are located is either submerged or angled away from the camera, making them impossible to verify.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey to greyish-black with distinctive white patches from barnacles and whale lice.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible skin clearly exhibits the characteristic mottled grey/black coloration with distinct white callosities and barnacle patches typical of grey whales.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: No dorsal fin present; multiple dorsal knuckles along posterior back.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The dorsal area (back) of the whale is not visible in this vertical head-shot composition.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Robust spindle-shaped body of enormous proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Only the head is visible; the full body shape cannot be assessed.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Flippers (pectoral fins) are broad and paddle-shaped, remarkably elongated relative to body size.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Pectoral fins are not visible in the frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail flukes are broad with smooth trailing edge and central notch.
